title: Pinchas of Habata (the stonecutter)
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: English translation and editorial notes prepared for Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: In the Sifrei (Emor, כה), it is said of him that his lot fell to become High Priest. The treasurers went and found him quarrying, and they filled the quarry for him with gold dinars. R. Ch. ben Gamliel said: “Was he a stonecutter? Was he not our son-in-law? They found him only plowing.”[^1] In the Tosefta, Yoma chapter 1, the reading is “Ish Chavata.”[^2]

notes.text: The personal name is abbreviated אר״ח בן גמליאל in the source. The introductory אמר (“said”) is clear from the sentence, but the name represented by ח is not identified here: “R. Ch.” retains that initial rather than guessing a full name. The earlier draft’s “Rabban Shimon” is withdrawn. כה״ג is the ordinary contextual abbreviation for High Priest. No new reading of the printed page is claimed.

The source labels its first reference ספרי אמור-כה, retained as “Sifrei (Emor, כה).” No correction to Sifra or modern section number is asserted without a checked witness. The Tosefta reference also remains unverified. The heading’s הבתה (Habata) and the cited variant חבתה (Chavata) are kept distinct; neither transliteration identifies a place with certainty.
